rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scale of divine mercy is beyond imagination and astonishes those who rely on visible means.
rows.anchor: those who are slaves to apparent resources are wonderstruck.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah's supplication had a proper objective, came at the right time with sincere emotion, and was accepted as soon as he made it.
rows.anchor: Zachariah’s supplication was also made with the correct objective, at the right time and with sincere emotions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word samiyy means a peer or example; God assures Zachariah that his child will have no parallel despite the parents' age and barrenness.
rows.anchor: These words are meant to assure Zacharias (sws) that though he has become old and his wife is barren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word atiyy means something exceeding limits and becoming uncontrollable; Zachariah voices doubts based on appearances to gain further assurance.
rows.anchor: Zacharias (sws) has expressed here his doubts viz the viz the apparent circumstances.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concomitant clues indicate a divine voice; the suppressed predicate after thus emphasizes that God's decision is destined, and creating a child is easy for the one who created from nothing.
rows.anchor: Concomitant indications show that this answer is given by a divine voice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah sought a sign for mental certainty that the glad tidings came from God rather than his own desire or Satan; prophetic caution about dreams and voices does not show weak faith.
rows.anchor: Since these glad tidings were a manifestation of his desire and had great importance for him, he wanted to have complete satisfaction.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign left Zachariah unable to speak to people while still able to remember God, showing a state caused by the Merciful rather than Satan; he emerged and gestured for people to glorify God.
rows.anchor: if a person is able to remember God through his tongue but cannot speak anything else

rows.speaker: some scholars
rows.claim: Some scholars read the phrase as a negative command to remain silent; Islahi rejects this reading because it overlooks why Zachariah requested a sign and why he was silenced.
rows.anchor: as a negative imperative and not just the portrayal of a state.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawiyy means free of defect or illness, so the silence was a divine sign in full health; the word does not mean continuous or consecutive and also occurs at 19:17.
rows.anchor: In other words, this state of Zacharias (sws) would not be because of a shortcoming or an ailment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Layāl encompasses both night and day, as ayyām does in 3:41; this is common Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: which also encompasses both day and night. This usage is common in Arabic.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mihrab denotes a worship room or veranda; Zachariah was at a place in the Temple, and 3:39 likewise shows he received the glad tidings while praying.
rows.anchor: that he received these glad tidings while he was praying.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah's gesture showed that a major providential secret was not yet ready to be disclosed, so people should wait and remember God meanwhile.
rows.anchor: His gesturing towards his people to glorify God also shows that he was harbouring a major secret of providence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book John was told to hold fast to is the Torah; Zachariah received no separate revealed Book.
rows.anchor: obviously refers to the Torah. No separate Book was revealed to Zacharias (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hukm is the ability to distinguish right from wrong; although it generally appears after maturity and peaks around forty, John received it in childhood.
rows.anchor: It refers to the power and ability to decide between right and wrong.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative compresses John's birth and growth to maturity before his prophethood; holding fast to God's Book meant guarding against Satan, his eternal enemy, and John ultimately sacrificed his life for it.
rows.anchor: He was blessed with prophethood from God and was directed by Him to hold fast to the Book of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanan means love, liveliness, and compassion; Islahi finds it strange that some attributed to Ibn Abbas ignorance of this common Arabic word.
rows.anchor: means love, liveliness and compassion. This word is a very common Arabic word and it is strange how some people have ascribed this opinion to Ibn ‘Abbās

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanan describes a living, vibrant heart and soul rather than an inert existence; John's quality was profound, as his Gospel statements still move people.
rows.anchor: This trait signifies that the heart and soul of a person are vibrant and living.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakāh here means purity and cleanliness, inward and outward, and reflects the inner compassion denoted by hanan.
rows.anchor: Obviously, this refers to both inner and outer purity. It is actually a reflection of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqī points to John's devout deeds and ascetic life: he publicly called people to repent, lived simply, and gave his life for God's Book.
rows.anchor: This word points to John’s (sws) deeds and character: he was devout and pious.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John remained faithful and obedient to his parents despite being able to think that his life and instruction depended only on God; he was never arrogant or defiant.
rows.anchor: he was never overcome with this notion and continued to be faithful and obedient to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels greeted John with peace and blessings at birth, death, and resurrection, giving him God's favor through every phase despite how people treated him in this world.
rows.anchor: welcomed him in every phase of life: the day he was born, the day he died

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John's story prefaces Jesus' birth and upbringing: as a predecessor and relative with a similar life, he prompts Christians to reconsider why they deify one of two consecutive prophets from the same family.
rows.anchor: By mentioning both of them together, the Almighty has invited the Christians to open their eyes

none: This segment contains only the verse passage and its translation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kitāb refers to the Gospels, where Mary's story appears in parts; since it was discussed under Āl-i Imrān, Islahi confines this section to its context.
rows.anchor: refers to the Gospels in which the anecdote of Mary has been narrated in parts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intibādh means seclusion; Mary withdrew for i'tikāf in the Temple's eastern women's court, and this association helps explain Christians' eastward prayer direction.
rows.anchor: This is because it was this side that was reserved for women for this purpose.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier reflects Mary's i'tikāf; God tested her by sending an angel in human form, an unusual appearance that confronted her without prior experience of divine communication, and her character was matchless.
rows.anchor: It seems that God wanted to test her when He sent an angel to her in the form of a human being.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's words display great poise and grace.
rows.anchor: These words reflect Mary’s great poise and grace.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel answered directly in order to allay Mary's fears.
rows.anchor: This answer by the angel was very direct to allay her fears.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word baghiy refers to a whore.
rows.anchor: The word ` refers to a whore.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects Luke's report that Mary was married to Joseph: if she were married, the news would have pleased her, and he attributes this account to Jewish opposition to Jesus' miraculous birth.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, this account of Luke’s Gospel is the result of some Jewish incursion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary had vowed Temple service, whose servants did not marry; even setting that tradition aside, her words fit a chaste virgin alone, and marriage would make her family's later rebuke baseless.
rows.anchor: Servants of the Temple never used to get married. For a moment, even if this tradition is ignored

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jidh means a tree's stem, and the definite article indicates Mary knew the palm; perhaps God had guided her in a dream to go there when labor began, where her needs would be met.
rows.anchor: she was guided in a dream from God to go to this tree when the time of birth arrives

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's words reveal the deep agony of a chaste woman from a noble family facing humiliation at her child's birth.
rows.anchor: The words of the verse reflect her deep agony.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller is the angel, and the phrase below her refers to the palm tree.
rows.anchor: these words were uttered by the angel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarī refers to a small spring that God made flow for Mary.
rows.anchor: Your Lord has made a stream to flow from below you.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though deeply distressed, Mary complained only to God and did not act wrongly in frustration; this was her test, after which extraordinary divine mercy appeared.
rows.anchor: Mary (sws) neither complained to anyone except God nor took a wrong step out of frustration.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The palm stem means a tree trunk; Mary's shaking it was only a pretext for God's mercy, since a touch was enough for dates to fall as if summoning food.
rows.anchor: Shaking it was just an excuse for the mercy of God to appear; otherwise, how could she have had the power to solely do so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the angel told Mary to signal that she was fasting and would not speak, the source infers that he had instructed her to keep the fast; otherwise her message would be a lie.
rows.anchor: he must have directed her to fast; otherwise, how could he have asked her to lie.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The silent fast belonged to Jewish law and could be observed in any condition, explaining how Mary could keep it while in labor; scripture also uses silence for remembrance and worship.
rows.anchor: among the Jews the fast of mere silence was part of their law and this fast could be kept in every state.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, qāla can mean to gesture, as shown by common expressions for gesturing with a spear or hand.
rows.anchor: A word that implies “to gesture” should have been used. The answer to this question is that

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aaron addressed here is a reputable member of Mary's family, not Moses' brother; the source says several narratives establish this.
rows.anchor: Aaron here does not refer to the brother of Moses (sws). He is someone reputable from the family of Mary

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Mary had vowed silence, she gestured to Jesus to answer, evidently trusting God had made him able to defend her; once she passed the trial, divine mercy appeared.
rows.anchor: Mary (sws) had kept a fast of silence, she could not have said anything from her mouth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's trial required the child in her arms to testify to her innocence and chastity and silence the people.
rows.anchor: was essential that the child in her lap bear witness to her innocence and chastity so that everyone is silenced.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus first calls himself God's servant so no one mistakes his miraculous birth for superhuman status; Hebrew ben can mean servant or son, and Paul later used the ambiguity to invent the Trinity.
rows.anchor: In other words, what he intended to say was that no one should be misled by the miraculous nature of his birth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus received a divine Book and prophethood and became a source of good; he followed, preached, and revived Moses' law while adding wisdom, preserved in scattered Gospel counsels.
rows.anchor: Jesus (sws) followed and practiced the sharī‘ah brought by Moses (sws), and also preached and revived it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and zakāh are religion's two foundational directives: despite different outward forms, prayer joins people to God and zakāh connects them to fellow humans, so dismantling either collapses religious practice.
rows.anchor: It is primarily these two directives which are the foundation of all religions and sharī‘ah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' obedience to his mother shows that special birth and favors did not make him less human; he was a dutiful son, and the author says contrary Gospel portrayals were inserted to support his divinity claim.
rows.anchor: even though he had been born in a very special manner and had also been blessed with special favours from his Lord, he was still a son of his mother

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' peace at birth, death, and resurrection parallels John's and shows that Jesus too passed and will pass through each human life phase; weak reports cannot override this, and the Qur'an supports no contrary claim.
rows.anchor: just as every human being passes through all these phases of life, Jesus (sws) too passed and will pass through these phases.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 34–35 are God's parenthetical reminder within Jesus' speech, restating the facts Jesus himself gave.
rows.anchor: These two verses are from God and as parenthetical sentences are inserted within the speech of Jesus (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for disputing derives from fully milking a goat and came to describe magnifying a small issue into doubts and suspicions.
rows.anchor: this word began to be used for creating an issue out of something very small and in creating various doubts and suspicions in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's statement that He does not take offspring refutes Christian polytheism; Jesus' miraculous birth expresses the divine Be command, not divinity, since God needs only to command and create.
rows.anchor: Concealed in these words is also the message that the miraculous birth of Jesus (sws) is not an evidence of his divinity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 36 ends Jesus' speech after the parenthetical clarification; the Qur'an corrects Gospel phrases my father and your father to mean Lord, since otherwise all people would be God's children and Jesus would not be distinct.
rows.anchor: The context determines the meaning in which it is used.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next section rebukes Christian disagreements and warns that on the Day of Judgment God will expose every person's thoughts and deeds, while people are heedless now.
rows.anchor: In these few verses, the Christians are rebuked on their mutual differences. They warn people of a day in which every thought and deed of a person will be exposed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the truth about Jesus was clear, Christians differed and formed sects; Islahi identifies Simon Peter's followers as the few who held truth, believed in Muḥammad and the Qur'an, and were praised by it.
rows.anchor: Only a few among them who were the followers of Simon Peter adhered to the truth.
